SMTO-SKL-0130 — Slack won't let SMTO delete that message

GUID: e2720922-3101-5cff-b3a8-55def6dc9723
Slug: slack-cannot-delete-message
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack refused to delete the message, usually because the connected account didn't post it or your workspace doesn't allow it. The message is still there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Slack, check who posted the message. SMTO can usually delete only messages posted by the account or bot it's connected as. Slack's rules decide who may delete each message.
  2. Ask your Slack workspace admin whether your account is allowed to delete messages. Some workspaces let only admins delete messages.
  3. If you're allowed and still want it gone, check in Slack that the message is still there. Then ask the Agent to delete it again, or delete it yourself in Slack. Once Slack's rules allow it, a new delete request can work; SMTO asks you to confirm it because deleting is permanent.

What success looks like

  • The message no longer appears in Slack, or you've decided to keep it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your Slack workspace admin, who controls the deletion rules.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned cant_delete_message for chat.delete on the exact channel_id and ts.

What this means

  • Slack returns cant_delete_message for the exact deletion request. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns cant_delete_message for the exact deletion request.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect ownership and deletion policy for the exact channel and timestamp.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the message author matches the profile's user_id or bot_user_id and that the workspace's deletion policy permits it for this principal; resubmit slack.delete_message only with the exact channel_id and ts after confirming the message still exists.
  • Verify message ownership and workspace deletion policy; use exact channel_id and ts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The authorized deletion is deliberate and permitted, or the message is left intact.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
